article.title: Market Fish Resources in Magallanes, Sorsogon, Philippines
article.affiliationAsPublished: Fisheries Department, Sorsogon State University - Magallanes Campus
article.access: Official PJS landing page and PDF were indexed but direct retrieval returned 403. Reviewed the full article text from an author-uploaded ResearchGate copy and cross-checked the abstract against the DOST-published PJS landing-page result.
article.reuse: No item-specific article license was identified in the reviewed publisher/index text. No PDF, table image or article file retained; publication reuse remains unapproved.

studyScope.marketLocation: Central public market, Poblacion, Magallanes, Sorsogon; article reports 12°49'40" N, 123°50'0" E.
studyScope.methodSummary: Authors assembled common-name records from LGU and BFAR offices, validated a roster through a semi-structured survey of vendors and peddlers, determined reported origin/seasonal availability, and identified fish by gross morphology using regional atlases and FishBase 2022.
notSupported: No exact capture event, fishing vessel, landing event, gear, capture coordinates, specimen/voucher accession or source-area method crosswalk for each market specimen is established by the checklist.
The market record is not evidence of occurrence in Incarizan River or any specific freshwater/estuarine reach.
The paper is not a diet/prey or bait-suitability study.

manualOriginCodeCountFromTableText.method: Counted the table's numeric origin code for each of 77 numbered rows in the author-uploaded searchable full-text copy; verify against the publisher's page image before reuse.

claimsAsReported.temporalAvailabilityClaim: Authors report variation by monsoon; they explicitly say the seasonality data for the fishing grounds is not complete and only commercially available market fish were reported.
claimsAsReported.interpretation: The 77 names and table-origin categories are exact-source research transcriptions, not normalized taxa, newly created occurrence records, or complete regional fish inventory.

qualityFlags.issue: The prose's source-area counts (11 Ticao-Burias-only, 4 Sorsogon-Bay-only, 61 shared) total 76, while the article reports 77 taxa. Counting the table origin codes gives 10, 4 and 63 (77 total).
qualityFlags.decision: Preserve both as conflicting article claims. Do not use these derived source-area counts until the table is checked visually or clarified by the authors.

qualityFlags.issue: The prose says seven common names are used for multiple species but lists twelve names in that same sentence.
qualityFlags.decision: Do not create one-to-one vernacular-to-species mapping from the paper; treat local-name mapping as potentially ambiguous.

qualityFlags.issue: The table states broad fishing-ground origin areas, not exact catch coordinates or collection events; authors also identify differing methods/efforts as a barrier to comparing checklists.
qualityFlags.decision: Store as market-resource evidence only. Never map all 77 names to the market point, Sorsogon Bay polygon, Ticao-Burias Pass polygon, or Incarizan River as species occurrences.

qualityFlags.issue: Species identifications were made by gross morphology against atlases and FishBase 2022; no taxon-specific vouchers or public event-by-specimen dataset was located in the article.
qualityFlags.decision: Keep the article's names verbatim as dated literature claims and run any future normalization against current authoritative taxonomic references.

nextAction: Keep the 77 taxa in the regional research inventory as market-sourced evidence with source-area and time limits, but do not promote them to occurrence/app rows. Resolve the 76-versus-77 and vernacular-count conflicts with the article page/table or authors before using its derived subsets. Continue with separately documented river/lake and coastal field datasets.
